newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Fokker says Samsung in exclusive probe.
newsitem.headline: Fokker says Samsung in exclusive probe.

text.p: The receivers of bankrupt planemaker Fokker NV said on Friday South Korea's Samsung is carrying out an exclusive due diligence at the Dutch firm.

"The focal point of this probe is the question whether all parties involved (among which governments, Stork, banks and the court-appointed receivers) can agree with a business plan currently being finalised by Samsung," Fokker said in a brief statement.
Fokker went bankrupt on March 15 this year after parent company Germany's Daimler Benz Aerospace cut a cash lifeline in February.

The receivers said they could not give further details. In August Samsung returned to Fokker headquarters in Amsterdam and the government in the Hague to talk about buying the Dutch company, after the South Korean firm dropped out of an Asian aircraft building project in June.
Samsung had carried out takeover talks on two earlier occasions, one prior to Fokker's collapse and one immediately after it.
The profitable maintenance and services arms of Fokker, Fokker Aviation, were sold to engineering equipment maker Stork in July.
This company agreed it would sell back these parts of Fokker if the survival or rebirth of the core aircraft manufacturing unit depended on it.
Stork said in August it was involved in the Samsung talks and that selling Fokker Aviation to the South Korean company was not an issue.
